items.followUp: State one difference between aerobic respiration and fermentation.

rubric.why: Oxygen availability distinguishes aerobic from anaerobic respiration.
rubric.description: Correctly contrasts aerobic respiration in the presence of oxygen with anaerobic respiration without oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the oxygen conditions for both processes.

rubric.why: The processes differ in the extent of glucose breakdown and the energy released.
rubric.description: Contrasts complete with incomplete breakdown, or greater with lower energy release.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct contrast in breakdown or energy yield.

modelAnswer: Aerobic respiration takes place in the presence of oxygen, whereas anaerobic respiration takes place without oxygen.
Aerobic respiration completely breaks down glucose and releases more energy; anaerobic respiration breaks it down incompletely and releases less energy.

rubric.why: Two valid examples earn the first mark toward the required four sources.
rubric.description: Gives two distinct valid sources of lipids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two distinct correct sources.

rubric.why: A complete set of four valid examples answers the question fully.
rubric.description: Gives four distinct valid sources of lipids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for four distinct correct sources.

modelAnswer: Four sources of lipids are butter, ghee, vegetable oils and nuts.

items.followUp: Describe one role of transpiration in the upward movement of water in plants.

rubric.why: Water loss from leaves creates a pull that helps move water upward through the plant.
rubric.description: States that transpiration creates a pull.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning transpiration pull.

rubric.why: Transpiration supports the movement of water and dissolved minerals from roots to leaves.
rubric.description: Links transpiration to the transport of water, with minerals, through the plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly linking transpiration to water or mineral transport.

modelAnswer: Transpiration creates a pull that helps transport water and dissolved minerals from the roots to the leaves.
